title: Judge blocks FCC's early review of Disney's ABC licenses
h1: Federal judge blocks the FCC's early review of Disney's ABC station licenses, citing free speech
description: U.S. District Judge Loren AliKhan on November 25, 2026 blocked the FCC's early review of Disney's ABC station licenses, calling it retaliation for speech.
standfirst: The preliminary injunction stops the license reviews while Disney's lawsuit continues. The judge also refused the government's request to throw the case out.
keywords: ABC FCC ruling, Disney FCC lawsuit, Judge Loren AliKhan, ABC broadcast licenses, Brendan Carr ABC, First Amendment broadcast license
takeaways: The preliminary injunction was filed Wednesday, November 25, 2026, in U.S. District Court.
The judge counted 11 calls by President Trump over two years for ABC to lose its licenses, the latest in July 2026.
FCC broadcast licenses usually run eight years and are reviewed on a staggered schedule; Disney's were all put under review at once.
body: A federal judge has stopped the Federal Communications Commission from pressing ahead with an early review of the broadcast licenses for ABC's local stations. In a preliminary injunction filed Wednesday, November 25, 2026, U.S. District Judge Loren AliKhan found the reviews were retaliation for satire, commentary and news coverage that President Donald Trump disliked, NPR reported. She also denied the administration's motion to dismiss the lawsuit brought by ABC and its parent, the Walt Disney Co.

According to NPR, the ruling leaned on public statements and social media posts by Trump and by FCC Chairman Brendan Carr. The judge counted 11 times in the past two years that Trump called for ABC to lose its licenses, most recently in July 2026. "Chairman Carr has taken President Trump's rhetoric as his marching orders," she wrote, as quoted by NPR.

The FCC had argued that the court could not act because the agency had not yet refused any renewal. The judge rejected that, finding that an early review opened for retaliatory reasons is itself unlawful, NPR reported. Licenses normally last eight years and come up on a staggered schedule. Disney's were placed under review all at once, and some were not due for several years.

ABC called the ruling an important victory for the First Amendment, NPR reported. Carr did not respond to NPR's request for comment. He has said the review grew out of concerns that Disney's diversity practices amounted to racial discrimination, and told NPR in August that the lawsuit had no merit.

The FCC's one Democratic commissioner, Anna M. Gomez, welcomed the decision in a statement posted by the agency. "This decision shows that this FCC is a paper tiger whose threats crumble when challenged by those willing to defend their rights," she said.

The injunction is preliminary, so it holds while the case proceeds. Disney's stations serve six of the 10 largest U.S. markets, according to NPR. In a separate case six weeks ago, another federal judge issued an injunction over White House access for CNN, MS NOW and Politico; the administration is appealing that ruling.

faq.q: What did the judge rule in the ABC and FCC case?
faq.a: On November 25, 2026, U.S. District Judge Loren AliKhan issued a preliminary injunction blocking the FCC's early review of Disney's ABC station licenses and declined to dismiss Disney's lawsuit.

faq.q: Why was the FCC reviewing ABC's licenses early?
faq.a: FCC Chairman Brendan Carr has said the review stemmed from concerns about Disney's diversity practices. The judge found it was retaliation for speech the administration disliked, according to NPR.
